evals.prompt: I have a Postgres schema for our e-commerce shop in shop_schema.sql (in your working directory). Create an OKF (Open Knowledge Format) knowledge bundle documenting this schema at ./shop-kb — one concept per table, plus whatever structure a good bundle needs.
evals.expected_output: A conformant OKF bundle: every concept .md has YAML frontmatter with non-empty type, one-sentence descriptions, schema tables matching the DDL, cross-links between related tables, index.md files, and a log.md.
assertions: okf.py validate on shop-kb reports 0 errors (parseable frontmatter + non-empty type everywhere)
all four DDL tables (customers, products, orders, order_items) have a concept document in the bundle
okf.py validate reports 0 warnings (no missing descriptions, no broken links)
bundle root contains an index.md listing the bundle contents
bundle contains a log.md whose entries use ISO YYYY-MM-DD date headings
concept documents cross-link related tables (e.g. orders links to customers) with resolvable markdown links
each table concept has a # Schema section covering the columns from the DDL

evals.prompt: In your working directory there's an OKF knowledge bundle at ./ga4 documenting the GA4 BigQuery sample dataset. Add a new metric concept 'purchase_conversion_rate' (share of users who triggered a purchase event, i.e. purchasers / total users) alongside the existing metrics, and make sure the bundle stays consistent and up to date.
evals.expected_output: New concept at ga4/references/metrics/purchase_conversion_rate.md with frontmatter (type Reference, one-sentence description, tags), SQL example, style matching sibling metrics; references/metrics/index.md updated; log entry added; bundle still validates with 0 errors.
assertions: ga4/references/metrics/purchase_conversion_rate.md exists with frontmatter containing type and a one-sentence description
ga4/references/metrics/index.md lists the new purchase_conversion_rate metric
okf.py validate on the modified ga4 bundle reports 0 errors
the new concept contains a fenced sql example expressing purchasers / total users
the new concept's style matches sibling metrics (type Reference, tags include metric, prose + sql + citations shape)
no pre-existing ga4 documents were broken (all previously present concept files still exist and validate)

evals.prompt: There's a knowledge bundle at ./ga4 in your working directory. Using only that bundle, explain how I'd compute the average spend per purchase-session for each user: which table(s) and fields are involved, and what does the bundle say the calculation is? Write your answer to answer.md and cite the bundle documents you used.
evals.expected_output: answer.md correctly derived from ga4/references/metrics/avg_spend_per_purchase_session_by_user.md and tables/events_.md (events_ table, ecommerce.purchase_revenue / purchase sessions per user), citing those concept paths.
assertions: answer.md exists in the run's outputs directory
answer.md identifies the events_ table as the data source
answer.md mentions the key fields: ecommerce.purchase_revenue (or purchase revenue), user_pseudo_id and ga_session_id session grouping, and event_name = 'purchase'
answer.md states the calculation per the bundle: AVG of per-session purchase spend, grouped per user
answer.md cites bundle document paths it used (the avg_spend_per_purchase_session_by_user metric and/or events_ table doc)
the ga4 bundle was not modified (read-only task)
